brief_description: Remove limiting elements on Tulucay-Napa #2 60 kV line to match the conductor rating of 1126 AMPS
driver_detail: Category P0 overload on Tulucay-Napa #2 60 kV line starting in 2024 (not present in 2021 baseline). Limiting switches and jumpers at Basalt and Tulucay substations have ratings below the conductor rating of 1126 Amps. Overloads worsen in high CEC forecast sensitivity, indicating load growth contribution alongside equipment limitation.
load_growth_evidence: Overload appears starting in 2024 (not in 2021 baseline) and worsens in high CEC forecast sensitivity, indicating that increasing load is driving the P0 overload on top of the existing equipment rating gap.

project_name: East Shore 230 kV Bus Terminals Reconfiguration
driver_detail: Category P2 overload on East Shore 230/115 kV transformer #1 due to simultaneous loss of San Mateo-East Shore 230 kV line and parallel transformer #2. Current bus configuration concentrates load on a single transformer under P2 contingency. Project reconfigures Russell City-East Shore and San Mateo-East Shore 230 kV lines at the bus to mitigate the concentration. Need date 2021 indicates an existing bus configuration deficiency, not load growth.

project_name: Newark 230/115 kV Transformer Bank #7 Circuit Breaker Addition
brief_description: Add second high-side circuit breaker to Newark 230/115 kV transformer bank #7
driver_detail: Category P2 overload on Newark 230/115 kV Transformer #11 caused by loss of parallel transformer #7 and associated 230 kV lines. Transformer #7 lacks a high-side circuit breaker, so the P2 contingency causes uncontrolled tripping that overloads transformer #11. Adding the missing breaker is terminal equipment completion, not a load growth response. Need date 2021 confirms existing equipment deficiency.
alternatives_rejected: Install a 230/115 kV transformer bank connecting to Newark 230 kV bus section E March 25, 2020

brief_description: Add sectionalizing breakers and a bus tie breaker to Moraga 230 kV bus
driver_detail: Category P2 contingency overloads on Oakland D-L 115 kV cable, Sobrante-Claremont 115 kV line, and 230 kV lines in Contra Costa-Newark corridor. Current Moraga 230 kV bus lacks sectionalizing breakers and a bus-tie breaker, causing P2 contingencies to propagate overloads across multiple facilities. The project adds these breakers to sectionalize the bus. Need date 2021 indicates an existing bus configuration deficiency.

brief_description: Reconductor ~9 circuit miles between Wilson and El Nido Substations
driver_detail: Category P2 (including P2-1, P2-2, P2-4) overloads on Wilson-El Nido 115 kV section present in ALL baseline summer peak scenarios (2021, 2024, 2029) and sensitivity scenarios. The conductor's summer emergency rating is exceeded up to 124% under the worst P2-1 contingency. Because overloads exist even in the 2021 near-term baseline, this is an existing conductor capacity deficiency rather than a load-growth-driven future issue. Reconductoring to at least 650 Amps addresses the structural capacity gap.

brief_description: • Upgrade Bank Breaker CB 52 and associated switches • Upgrade Borden 70 kV Bus Section “D”
objectives: Mitigate P3, P6 contingency driven overload
driver_detail: Category P1 (appearing in 2024), P3, and P6 overloads on Borden 230/70 kV Transformer Bank #1. Bank Breaker CB 52 and 70 kV Bus Section D are rated below the transformer bank's full capacity (200 N / 220 E MVA), preventing the transformer from operating at its design rating. The project upgrades the breaker and bus section to match the transformer's full capacity. The core issue is terminal equipment limitation rather than load growth.

objectives: Mitigate P1, P3 contingency driven overload
driver_detail: Category P1 and P3 contingency overloads on Salinas-Firestone 60 kV lines requiring reconductoring to at least 600 Amps summer emergency rating. Project need date is 2021, indicating overloads exist in the current system rather than being driven by future load growth. The conductor upgrade addresses an existing capacity deficiency on these 60 kV distribution-level transmission lines serving the Salinas area.

project_name: Pardee-Sylmar No. 1 and No. 2 230 kV Line Rating Increase Project
brief_description: The project involves replacing circuit breakers and other terminal equipment at SCE’s Pardee Substation and LADWP’s Sylmar Substation to increase the rating of the lines to match the rating of the line conductors.
objectives: The project is proposed to mitigate overload under P1, P3 and P6 contingency conditions. The project has a benefit-to-cost ratio (BCR) of 10.3–13.6.
driver_detail: Severe P1, P3, and P6 overloads on Sylmar-Pardee No. 1 and No. 2 230 kV lines in 2025 and 2029 summer peak cases. The system is stressed by the retirement of ~5,160 MW of OTC and nuclear generation by end of 2020, combined with solar unavailability during the evening peak hour. Terminal equipment (circuit breakers) at Pardee and Sylmar substations are rated below the conductor rating (2B-1590 ACSR); the project replaces breakers to match conductor capacity, increasing emergency ratings by 45%. BCR of 10.3–13.6 qualifies as economic benefit. Type is 'Reliability (with economic benefits)'.
alternatives_rejected: - Pacific Transmission Expansion (PTE) Project Maintaining sufficient local capacity March 25, 2020

brief_description: Upgrading VEA’s existing 138 kV Gamebird substation by adding a new 230/138 kV transformer and looping GLW’s Pahrump – Sloan Canyon 230 kV line into the upgraded Gamebird substation
objectives: The proposed project would mitigate the Amargosa bank overloads, 138 kV low voltage issues and Pahrump 230/138 kV bank overloads described in Appendix B. Summer
driver_detail: Thermal overloads on Amargosa 230/138 kV transformer and 138 kV low voltage issues following multiple Category P1, P4, P6, and P7 contingencies. The report explicitly states: 'Load growth in the VEA area was found to be the primary driver behind this reliability issue' and notes 'VEA is the area with the highest load growth in CAISO.' Overloads and low voltage issues appear across 2021, 2024, and 2029 study scenarios and worsen with the high-load forecast. New residential and commercial construction is forecasted to increase demand in Pahrump and Thousandaire areas.
load_growth_evidence: The report explicitly states: 'Load growth in the VEA area was found to be the primary driver behind this reliability issue.' VEA is identified as the area with the highest load growth in CAISO. Overloads appear in 2021 baseline and worsen in higher-load sensitivity scenarios, confirming load growth as the cause.
alternatives_rejected: A new Charleston – Vista 138 kV line Amargosa 230/138 transformer upgrade Carpenter Canyon – Charleston 230 kV project Energy storage at Sandy 138 kV substation
